newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: LITHUANIAN SHARES EDGE UP, MAZHEIKIU LEAPS.
newsitem.headline: LITHUANIAN SHARES EDGE UP, MAZHEIKIU LEAPS.

text.p: Official list shares maintained their slow rise on the Vilnius bourse on Tuesday, and Mazheikiu Nafta leapt by 15 percent as the market responded to its solid first half results, dealers said.
Central market volume approached 1.5 million litas and the official list index inched up 5.97 points to 1121.42. The broader group A index rose 28.57 points to 1904.05 points.
"Lately we have noticed bigger buyers coming to the bourse and they tend to invest in the official list shares and that pushes the rest of the market," one dealer said.

Mazheikiu Nafta refinery rocketed to 14 litas from 12.15 litas on turnover of 207,000 litas on the central market and the firm registered business of 60,000 litas in block trades at prices ranging from 12.00 to 14.00 litas.
"Mazheikiu Nafta's price rise was fuelled by its good results...after a long break the company reported a profit," Arvydas Jacikevichius of Suprema brokerage told Reuters.
The company reported an 18.2 million litas profit for the first half of the year.
Dealers said that interest in the refinery was also prompted by the government's plans to privatise it.
Vilniaus Bank inched up to 306 litas from 305.1 litas on turnover of 319,000 litas, while Hermis bank stayed steady at 267 litas on turnover of 224,000 litas.
Dealers said they were not expecting abrupt changes in the sector.
